extracted.intended_audience: feature journalists, reporters, and feature writers (including journalism students and newsroom feature editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing/newsworthiness-evaluating feature journalism: what makes feature stories special and the essential ingredients reporters should include. Focused on narrative, character, scene, theme, and utility across feature subtypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of celebration / sharing of journalistic platform
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features should celebrate or amplify people/communities — use the platform to share underrepresented or important voices and to lift up subjects rather than only expose or criticize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: Why this story now? Stakes that compel attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong feature explains why it matters at this moment and what stakes or timeliness compel reader attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait of the human experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story should use specific people and situations to illuminate broader human truths so readers can connect emotionally and intellectually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character (essential ingredient)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select central figures who are engaging, complex, and capable of carrying the story; the character should anchor reader interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action (essential ingredient)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include scenes and concrete actions — show events unfolding rather than only summarizing; use scene-building to create momentum and narrative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (essential ingredient)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground the narrative in a specific setting or place to provide texture, context, and sensory detail that anchors readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme (essential ingredient)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the piece conveys a larger thematic resonance or meaning that ties scenes and character to broader ideas or societal questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature categories (formats/types)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable/recognized feature forms include: feature beat writing portfolios (three stories on one specialty: arts, fashion, food, health, religion, technology, travel), narrative video features, utility features (practical explainers), profile writing, and trend pieces — choose the format appropriate to the story's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong central character / subject (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear, strong central subject who drives the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of a strong, central subject is a key indicator of a feature's newsworthiness and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid scene-building (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of scenes to create vivid, concrete storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective features rely on scene-setting and concrete detail rather than abstract exposition to draw readers in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional truth (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest emotional portrayal that resonates with readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey genuine emotional stakes and authenticity — emotional truth helps readers connect and trust the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larger thematic resonance (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should speak to bigger ideas beyond its particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features should illuminate broader social, cultural, or human themes through the specifics of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility (in service features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate readers about topics affecting daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For service/utility features, usefulness and clear takeaways are key — the piece should help readers act or understand practical matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural/social significance (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance to culture or society at large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories gain newsworthiness when they reflect or illuminate important cultural or social issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recognizably individual or editorial voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distinctive narrative voice helps set a feature apart and engages readers; voice should suit the subject and publication.
